about: From scratch to the top (docs/specs/built-to-last.md, section 5; queue built-to-last): four stages, each with one question, and one North Star target per life area and stage. Targets are planning rules in common use, paraphrased, verified on the date shown and re-checked by the review date. A country can change a number, so each target says where to confirm and carries a 'where' tag. Not financial, medical or legal advice. Not yet read by the app: briefs B16 and B17 wire it in.
rule: A person has a stage per area: the highest stage whose targets, and all earlier ones, are met. The overall stage is the lowest of the five, because the weakest area is the constraint. Show one next target, for the weakest area.

stages.title: Survive
stages.question: Could one bad month break us?

stages.title: Stabilise
stages.question: Is the floor solid enough to stop worrying?

stages.title: Grow
stages.question: Is each year clearly better than the last?

stages.title: Compound
stages.question: Does it now grow without my effort?

targets.title: 1 month of essential costs in the bank
targets.confirm: Your own bank statements

targets.title: No new high-interest debt
targets.confirm: Your card and loan statements; high interest here means a card balance carried over or an unsecured loan

targets.title: Health cover in force for everyone at home
targets.confirm: Your policy papers or your employer's benefits page

targets.title: 6 months of essential costs set aside
targets.confirm: A common planning range is 3 to 6 months; more if income is uneven

targets.title: High-interest debt at zero
targets.confirm: Your card and loan statements

targets.title: Saving 20% of take-home pay
targets.confirm: A common budgeting rule (50/30/20); your own numbers decide

targets.title: Life cover where someone depends on your income
targets.confirm: A common planning rule is 10 to 15 times yearly income plus loans; compare on insurers' own sites

targets.title: Saving 30% of take-home pay
targets.confirm: Your own numbers; a stretch target, not a rule

targets.title: Investments worth 5 to 10 years of costs
targets.confirm: Your statements; count only what is invested for the long term

targets.title: Investments worth 25 to 33 years of costs
targets.confirm: From the 4% withdrawal rule of thumb; it was derived from United States market history, so check it for your country with a registered adviser

targets.title: Investments worth 30 to 33 years of costs
targets.confirm: A more careful multiple often used where inflation runs higher; check with a SEBI-registered investment adviser

targets.title: 7 hours of sleep on 5 nights a week
targets.confirm: Public sleep guidance for adults is 7 hours or more a night; your doctor if sleep is poor

targets.title: 150 minutes of movement a week
targets.confirm: World Health Organization guidance for adults: 150 to 300 minutes of moderate activity a week

targets.title: One baseline check-up done
targets.confirm: Your doctor decides which tests fit your age and history

targets.title: 150 to 300 minutes a week, plus strength work on 2 days
targets.confirm: World Health Organization guidance for adults

targets.title: A check-up every year, and your key numbers known
targets.confirm: Your doctor names the numbers that matter for you (often blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol, waist)

targets.title: Every key number in its healthy range for 3 years running
targets.confirm: Your doctor sets the range for you

targets.title: The same numbers held for 10 years, with a recovery week each quarter
targets.confirm: Your doctor

targets.title: Income steady for 3 months
targets.confirm: Your own bank statements

targets.title: One page that says what you are good at
targets.confirm: Your own records

targets.title: One skill others pay for, proven by a result
targets.confirm: A result someone else can name

targets.title: Pay at the market rate for your work
targets.confirm: Two published salary surveys for your role and city, or three peers

targets.title: Income from 2 sources
targets.confirm: Your own records; check your employment contract before taking outside work

targets.title: Known for one thing in your field
targets.confirm: People outside your team ask you about it

targets.title: Work chosen for meaning, and 2 people you have raised up
targets.confirm: Your own judgement

targets.title: Everyone knows who to call and where the papers are
targets.confirm: Your own records; the family emergency file in the council data

targets.title: A nominee named on every account and policy
targets.confirm: Each bank, fund house and insurer

targets.title: A signed will
targets.confirm: A lawyer for anything beyond a simple estate; rules differ by country and faith

targets.title: 3 unhurried hours together each week
targets.confirm: Your own calendar

targets.title: A yearly family review, and one shared goal reached each year
targets.confirm: Your own records

targets.title: A succession plan reviewed every year, with the next generation running part of it
targets.confirm: A lawyer and a tax professional in each country where the family holds assets

targets.title: 20 minutes on 5 days a week
targets.confirm: Your own ticks

targets.title: One course or book finished each quarter, and used
targets.confirm: Your own records

targets.title: One hard skill a year, shown in public work
targets.confirm: Work someone else can see

targets.title: You teach it, and your notes outlive the week
targets.confirm: Your own judgement

sources.note: 150 to 300 minutes of moderate activity a week, and muscle strengthening on 2 or more days

sources.who: Retirement research on United States market history
sources.note: The source of the 25 times multiple; a rule of thumb, not a promise, and weaker outside the market it was drawn from

sources.what: Emergency fund, saving rate and life cover multiples
sources.note: Ranges in general use; a registered adviser confirms them for one person
